claims.text: A section runs to the next heading of EQUAL OR HIGHER level, so an H2 contains its H3s -- the same containment a Python function has over its nested defs (``_units_from_tree`` emits both).
claims.why: The loop at lines ~753-758 sets end to the index of the next heading with level <= current level, implementing exactly that containment.

claims.text: ``distilled`` False means the raw document was returned because no skeleton of it was SMALLER than the document itself (a short README, a doc that is nothing but headings). Returning the raw text there is the honest outcome: the alternative is a 'distillation' that grows the prompt, which this repo has already measured as a lie and pinned with a test.
claims.why: The logic for setting distilled False is not in this chunk; the dataclass only defines the field, not the construction logic.
The field is defined with default 'full' and the docstring lists the possible values.

claims.text: internal_links: (resolved rel targets, unresolved count). Sorted, de-duplicated, self excluded -- a document linking to itself is not an edge.
claims.why: The function returns sorted(resolved) and unresolved, excludes self (target != parse.document), and uses a set for deduplication.

claims.text: parse_document: Parse one Markdown document into sections (the hierarchy) and links.
claims.why: The function returns DocumentParse with sections (built from headings) and links (from _link_occurrences).

observations.what: The _slice helper uses line numbers as indices; assumes that lines list indices correspond to line numbers (1-indexed). Code uses line=idx+1 etc.
Title extraction: first H1, then any heading, then basename of document. May pick a non-H1 heading as title.
DocSkeleton.to_dict is defined but its body is cut off; the chunk ends after the opening brace.
